hook.h2: The first words He ever spoke were light
hook.text: Then our Father said, "Let there be light," and there was light.
hook.note: Open any other Bible at Genesis 1 and those four words look exactly like the sentence around them — the same black ink as the genealogies. Here they are blue, because our Father said them. That is the whole idea, and you can see it working from the third verse of the book. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking, and until now you had no way of knowing which.

short350: You have wanted a Father your whole life. Not a doctrine about Him. Not a distant power. A Father — His voice, His heart turned toward you.
Father's Heart Bible is the first Bible in print where you can see who is speaking.
Our Father's words in BLUE. The Son's in RED. The Spirit's in PURPLE.

For a hundred and twenty-five years, red letters have shown the Son speaking. Our Father speaks more than three times as often — 125,457 words across 5,623 verses — and every one of them has been printed in the same black ink as the genealogies. More than one word in four of the Bible is a divine person speaking. The color marks ownership, not quotation: His words stay His on any lips that carry them faithfully, words He never spoke are never colored, and narration stays black.
When His own asked how to pray, the Son did not give them a formula. He gave them a Father, and told them to say so out loud. Everything in this Bible follows from that one word.
That is what this Bible was made to do. Not to tell you about a Father who speaks, but to show you where He already has.

He is not distant. He is not disappointed. He is your Heavenly Father, and He delights in you as His beloved child. If father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you: the Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood, but the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

An introduction opens each book, a Father's note closes each with a short prayer, and 1,354 notes serve the reader, not the scholar. A presentation page carries their name. Six by nine, paperback and hardcover, full color throughout.
A fresh translation from the original Hebrew, Aramaic, and Greek — complete, 66 books and 31,085 verses. A gift, a keepsake, an heirloom.
Receive the Father. Hear His voice. His heart is for you.

If the word father is not a word of comfort for you, this Bible is especially for you. The Father revealed here is no projection of broken human fatherhood. He is the original, from whom every family in heaven and on earth takes its name.

faq.q: How is this different from the targeted editions?
faq.a: It is the same complete Bible and the same translation. The targeted editions — the Dad's Bible, the Teen Bible, the Soldier's Bible and the rest — carry a cover and opening pages written for one reader. This one names no audience. If you want a Bible that speaks to who someone is, choose a targeted edition. If you just want the Bible, this is it.

faq.q: Which cover color should I choose?
faq.a: They are identical inside. Charcoal is the quiet one and the most common choice for a personal copy; Plum reads warmer and is the one most often bought as a gift; White is the brightest on a shelf and photographs best for a presentation. Every color is available in paperback and hardback.

Paperback if you are going to carry it, mark it and not feel precious about it. Hardback if it is going into someone's hands as a gift, or onto a shelf for years. The interior is the same 876 pages in full color either way.

faq.q: Should I get regular or large print?
faq.a: They are different books. This edition is the complete Bible — 66 books, 1,189 chapters, 31,085 verses, with all 1,354 study notes. The Large Print edition sets the type larger for easier reading, and to do that it carries Genesis, Psalms, Proverbs and the entire New Testament in full, with the remaining 36 Old Testament books as an introduction with selected passages. Choose Large Print for readability; choose this one if you want every verse in full.

faq.q: Is the color really on every page?
faq.a: Yes — Genesis to Revelation, in full color throughout. Not a red-letter New Testament with a black Old Testament, and not a color section at the back. You can see it for yourself, free, at fathersheartbible.com/read.
